language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<meta>Beijing Kanjur woodblock print in red ink, pothi format, Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra (Erdeni čogčalaγsan / 大寶積經), Volume 2 (qa / 第二卷), folio 2a (degedü qoyar / 上二), opening of the Ārya-anantamukha-pariśodhana-nirdeśa-parivarta (Činadu kijaγar barasi ügei egüden-i masi tegüs üjegülügči).</meta>

<image-desc size="small" type="decorative" significance="low">Woodblock-printed double red border frame with floral scrollwork motifs enclosing the central text panel and two vertical marginal cartouches on the left and right.</image-desc>

<margin>ᠬᠠ ᠴᠣᠭᠴᠠᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</margin>
<margin>大寶積經第二卷上二</margin>

᠀ ᠨᠠ ᠮᠠ ᠮᠠ ᠾᠠ ᠶᠠ ᠨᠠ ᠰᠤᠳᠤᠷ᠎ᠠ ᠅
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠬᠢᠵᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠂ ᠪᠠᠷᠠᠰᠢ
ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠡᠭᠦᠳᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ
ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ ᠨᠡᠷᠡᠲᠦ ᠂ ᠶᠡᠬᠡ
ᠬᠥᠯᠭᠡᠨ ᠰᠤᠳᠤᠷ ᠅ ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ
ᠨᠥᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ
ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠣ᠎ᠠ ᠨᠠᠷ ᠯᠤᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠰᠡᠯᠲᠡ
ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠦ ᠮᠥᠷᠭᠦᠮᠦ ᠅ ᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ
ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠲᠤ ᠂
ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠥᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ
ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠠᠯᠭᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠲᠠᠰ ᠴᠣᠭᠴᠠᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠲᠡᠬᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ ᠦᠨ
ᠶᠡᠬᠡ ᠬᠤᠪᠠᠷᠠᠭ ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ
ᠲᠠᠪᠢᠨ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠲᠡᠬᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ
ᠯᠤᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠲᠤ ᠂ ᠴᠠᠭᠯᠠᠰᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠂
ᠲᠣᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠲᠣᠮᠰᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠣ᠎ᠠ
ᠨᠠᠷ ᠂ ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠲᠩᠷᠢ ᠨᠠᠷ ᠬᠦᠷᠢᠶᠡᠯᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ

<vocab>ᠴᠣᠭᠴᠠᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ, 大寶積經, ᠪᠠᠷᠠᠰᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠡᠭᠦᠳᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ, ᠶᠡᠬᠡ ᠬᠥᠯᠭᠡᠨ ᠰᠤᠳᠤᠷ, ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠥᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ, ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠣ᠎ᠠ, ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠠᠯᠭᠠᠰᠤᠨ, ᠲᠠᠰ ᠴᠣᠭᠴᠠᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ, ᠠᠶᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠲᠡᠬᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ, ᠬᠤᠪᠠᠷᠠᠭ, ᠲᠩᠷᠢ</vocab>

translation.text:
<meta>Beijing Kanjur woodblock print in red ink, pothi format, Maharatnakuta Sutra, Volume 2, folio 2a, opening of the Noble Sutra Teaching the Complete Accomplishment of the Inexhaustible Gate to the Ultimate Limit. The final clause continues onto the next folio.</meta>

<note>Woodblock-printed double red border frame with floral scrollwork motifs enclosing the central text panel and two vertical marginal cartouches on the left and right.</note>

<margin>Volume <term>Qa</term> <gloss>second letter of the Mongolian alphabet, designating Volume Two</gloss>, <term>Čogčalaγsan</term> <gloss>Heap of Jewels</gloss>, Upper, Two <note>original: "qa čogčalaγsan degedü qoyar"; marginal signature marking Volume 2 of the Maharatnakuta section, folio 2 recto</note></margin>
<margin>Great Heap of Jewels Sutra, Volume Two, Upper, Two <note>original: "大寶積經第二卷上二"</note></margin>

Homage to the Great Vehicle <term>sutra</term> <gloss>discourse of the Buddha</gloss>! <note>original: "na ma ma ha ya na sudur-a", a Mongolian phonetic transcription of the Sanskrit invocation "Namo Mahayanasutraya"</note>
The Great Vehicle <term>Sutra</term> <gloss>Discourse</gloss>
entitled Most Perfectly Revealing
the Inexhaustible Gate
to the Ultimate Limit <note>original: "Činadu kijaγar, barasi ügei egüden-i masi tegüs üjegülügči neretü, yeke kölgen sudur"; corresponding to the Sanskrit "Arya-anantamukha-parishodhana-nirdesha-parivarta-nama-mahayana-sutra"</note>.
To the <term>Ilaju tegüs nögčigsen burqan</term> <gloss>Victoriously Transcendent Buddha, translating Sanskrit Bhagavan Buddha</gloss>
together with all the
<term>bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>awakening beings</gloss>,
to them I bow in homage.
Thus have I heard
at one time:
the Victoriously Transcendent Buddha
was at the Royal City <note>original: "qaγan-u balγasun", the standard Mongolian translation of Rajagriha, capital of Magadha</note>,
on Vulture Peak Mountain <note>original: "tas čogčalaγsan aγulan-du", literally "Vulture-Heaped Mountain", translating Sanskrit Gridhrakuta</note>,
together with a great <term>qubarag</term> <gloss>monastic community, translating Sanskrit sangha</gloss>
of <term>ayaγ-a tekimlig</term> <gloss>fully ordained monks, an Old Uyghur loanword meaning "worthy of veneration", translating Sanskrit bhikshu</gloss>
numbering one thousand two hundred
and fifty monks,
and encircled by immeasurable,
innumerable <term>bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>awakening beings</gloss>
and by many <term>tngri</term> <gloss>celestial deities, translating Sanskrit deva</gloss>

<summary>This folio from Volume 2 of the Beijing Mongolian Kanjur opens the Sutra Most Perfectly Revealing the Inexhaustible Gate to the Ultimate Limit, a section of the Great Heap of Jewels Sutra. Following a Sanskrit invocation and homage to the Buddha and bodhisattvas, it sets the scene on Vulture Peak Mountain near Rajagriha, where the Buddha is surrounded by 1,250 monks, countless bodhisattvas, and celestial deities.</summary>
